extracted.intended_audience: cancer researchers and research organisations seeking to align with Cancer Research UK funding priorities
extracted.subtask_description: Organisation-level research strategy describing the priorities and criteria Cancer Research UK will use to fund and support cancer research across discovery, detection, prevention, clinical translation, data, and underserved cancer types; includes commitments on investment, equity, and patient/public involvement. Useful for researchers planning proposals or aligning programmes with CRUK strategic aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy four objectives (discover, detect, prevent, treat)
rubrics_metrics.description: It's built around four objectives – to discover, detect, prevent, and treat – so that progress in understanding the fundamental biology of cancer leads to new prevention measures, tests and treatments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advances in fundamental biology to drive prevention measures, diagnostic tests and therapeutic treatments; the strategy should connect discovery to downstream impact across these four objective areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery research
rubrics_metrics.description: Our discovery research portfolio provides fundamental insight into the mechanisms by which cancer develops, progresses and responds to treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise projects that deliver fundamental biological insight (mechanisms of development, progression, response) that can underpin future translational work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early detection and diagnosis
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re advancing transformative cancer outcomes through research focussed on early detection of cancer and pre-cancerous changes, underlying biology of cancers, cancer emergence and progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support work targeting earlier identification of cancer or pre-cancer, mechanistic studies of emergence and progression, and development of diagnostic approaches that change outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention and population research
rubrics_metrics.description: We support a wide range of prevention and population research aimed at understanding the epidemiology of cancer, cancer risk, incidence and survival and preventative interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund epidemiological studies, risk-factor research, survival analyses and intervention studies that seek to prevent cancer at the population level or reduce incidence and improve outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical research (pipeline and trial design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our robust portfolio of clinical studies spans the clinical pipeline, including early phase and first-in-human trials, ambitious and innovative trial design, and clinical infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise proposals across the clinical development continuum, with emphasis on novel/ambitious trial designs, first-in-human/early-phase work and strengthening of clinical infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research data (data science, analytics, curation and ethics)
rubrics_metrics.description: We aim to leverage the enormous potential of data science and advanced analytics by creating a research culture and community supporting timely, transparent and ethical curation and use of data in cancer research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect emphasis on timely and transparent data curation, ethical data use, and the application of data science/advanced analytics to answer important cancer research questions; build community and culture around data sharing and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancers of unmet need
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re building strong, sustainable research communities in notoriously hard-to-treat cancers such as brain, lung, oesophagus, pancreas, liver and stomach, and can support you as you move into this field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage proposals that focus on hard-to-treat ('unmet need') cancers; support community-building, capacity development and sustained programmes in these specific tumour types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's and young people's cancer
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re prioritising research in children's and young people's cancers to address the unique barriers researchers and partners face in driving progress in this area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise research that addresses age-specific biology, barriers to progress, and tailored interventions for children and young people with cancer; recognise distinct needs vs adult cancers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Therapeutic innovation and translation (Cancer Research Horizons)
rubrics_metrics.description: We're committed to driving therapeutic innovation in oncology through our translational arm, Cancer Research Horizons. We have expertise and capabilities to translate early concepts to patient benefit, encompassing deep cancer biology knowledge and extensive drug discovery experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support translational programmes that move early concepts toward patient benefit, leveraging drug discovery expertise and deep biological understanding; expect emphasis on clear pathways to translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment commitment (2022–2027)
rubrics_metrics.description: To achieve this, we will spend £1.5bn between 2022 and 2027, investing in creative people and transformational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates scale and timeframe of funding commitment; applicants should note the substantial investment window and align proposals to long-term strategic priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in creative people and transformational research
rubrics_metrics.description: Investing in creative people and transformational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding and support are targeted at researchers and teams with creativity and potential for transformational impact rather than only incremental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce cancer inequalities and improve outcomes for everyone
rubrics_metrics.description: We will support research to reduce cancer inequalities and improve outcomes for everyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals that address disparities in cancer incidence, access, outcomes or care across populations are prioritised; equity-focused research is an explicit strategic criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve people affected by cancer (patient and public involvement)
rubrics_metrics.description: And we’ll involve people affected by cancer in our work. Explore our commitment to patient and public involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and favour meaningful patient and public involvement in research planning, conduct and dissemination; involvement is part of the strategy and likely a consideration for funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisation strategy focus (making discoveries, driving progress, bringing hope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our strategy renews our focus on making discoveries, driving progress, bringing hope - leading us to a world where everybody can lead longer, better lives, free from the fear of cancer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic framing emphasises translational impact and patient benefit as ultimate goals; projects should articulate how they contribute to longer, better lives and reduced fear of cancer.
